usageNotes: Returns historical RRD metric data points (CPU, memory, disk I/O, network) for a specific QEMU VM. The `timeframe` parameter is required and determines the data resolution and range — shorter timeframes give finer granularity. Use `cf=AVERAGE` for trend analysis and `cf=MAX` for spike detection; omitting `cf` defaults to AVERAGE on most Proxmox versions. The VM must exist on the specified node and the caller needs `VM.Audit` on `/vms/{vmid}`.

examples.summary: Fetch last hour of average metrics for VM 101 on node pve1

tips: Data resolution decreases as timeframe increases (e.g. 'year' returns one point per week, 'hour' returns one point per minute).
RRD data lags real-time by up to one RRD step interval (~70 seconds for the hour timeframe); do not use for live monitoring.
If the VM was recently created or migrated, older timeframes may return sparse or empty arrays for the period before the VM existed on that node.
Use `cf=MAX` when alerting on peak resource usage; `cf=AVERAGE` smooths out transient spikes and is better for capacity trending.
